page: Amazon Web Services c8gb.8xlarge is a compute-optimized server powered by the Nitro hypervisor and custom AWS Graviton ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 processors. It features 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs running at 2.8 GHz with a single thread per core. The memory configuration consists of 64.0 GB of RAM, yielding a 2.0 GB per core ratio. Cache architecture includes 64 KB L1d, 2 MB L2, and 36 MB L3 cache. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, but provides a baseline network bandwidth of 67 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate top-tier memory performance, with uncached large-block read bandwidth reaching 391.76 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 185.65 GB/sec, both placing in the top 10% of tested systems. Multi-core performance is also strong, highlighted by a Geekbench multi-core score of 21681.0 and a Passmark database operations score of 47341.83. Single-core performance and integer operations, such as gzip compression and Geekbench text processing, fall into the average range. LLM inference speeds are moderate for small and medium models but show limitations on larger models, with text generation for a 70B model averaging 3.82 tokens/sec.

Given its ARM64 architecture and high core density without hyperthreading, the c8gb.8xlarge offers a resource-efficient profile for parallelized compute workloads. The absence of local storage means it relies on network-attached storage, which is supported by its 67 Gbps network interface. This server is highly suited for multi-threaded applications, software compilation, database operations, static web serving, and high-throughput memory-bound tasks, while being less optimal for heavy single-threaded execution or large-scale LLM inference.
